recent_posts.title: Coming Soon: The Professional Software Tester! – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: A software testing professional shares insights from their upcoming book about career guidance for testers. The featured chapter emphasizes the importance of identifying knowledge gaps, particularly when learning test automation. The author recounts their experience struggling with JSON formatting concepts and provides practical advice on using resources like W3Schools quizzes and AI prompts to discover and address skill gaps in programming and testing.

recent_posts.title: What Silo Can Teach Us About Tech Debt – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Technical debt management requires a systematic eight-step approach: awareness of the problem, building a business case for fixes, understanding risks, stakeholder planning, scope limitation, rollback preparation, communication, and team collaboration. Using examples from the AppleTV series Silo and real-world payment system migration, the process emphasizes the importance of treating tech debt fixes as critical projects that require careful planning and risk assessment to avoid system failures.

recent_posts.title: Are You Over-Engineering Your Tests? – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Software testers who learn to code sometimes over-engineer their automated tests. Four key warning signs include automating everything instead of keeping some tests manual, asserting too many things in single tests rather than creating atomic tests, over-abstracting code that makes tests hard to understand and maintain, and constantly switching to new testing tools when existing ones work fine. The goal should be reliable, efficient, readable, and maintainable test automation.

recent_posts.title: Five Reasons Why Documentation is Important – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Documentation in software testing is crucial for ensuring efficient team collaboration, preventing missed requirements, and maintaining test coverage. While not everyone enjoys writing documentation, leveraging the skills of those who excel at it and building time into schedules for documentation work can lead to better and easier-to-maintain records. These documents facilitate smooth operations, aid new team members, and ensure comprehensive product testing.

recent_posts.title: How Quality = Health – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Maintaining software quality is akin to personal health; it requires ongoing attention and adaptation. Common excuses for neglecting software health, such as the time-consuming nature of updating tests, the difficulty of learning new systems, and prioritizing feature releases over quality, can lead to larger issues down the line. By investing time in improving test automation, learning new organizational systems, and addressing technical debt, teams can enhance product quality and user experience.

recent_posts.title: Know Your Limits – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Understanding and testing size, type, and performance limits in your application is crucial for ensuring security and a positive user experience. Boundary testing goes beyond specified acceptance criteria to uncover potential vulnerabilities such as buffer overflow attacks. It's important to validate file types accurately and conduct load and stress testing to find performance thresholds. Always knowing your limits helps prevent user frustration and potential attacks.

recent_posts.title: New Year’s Resolutions for Testers – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Improve your software testing career in 2025 by learning test automation through a free YouTube course, reading recommended books on various testing topics, taking relevant online courses, attending virtual meetups and conferences, and acquiring new skills such as API Contract Testing. These activities will help you stay updated and enhance your testing abilities.

recent_posts.title: What Does Test Coverage Mean? – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Test coverage can refer to multiple aspects of software testing: code coverage, automation coverage, and feature coverage. It highlights that test coverage does not equate to testing every possible scenario to achieve 100%, which is unfeasible. Understanding what aspect of test coverage is being measured is crucial for accurate assessments.

recent_posts.title: Five Quality Changes to Make When Your Company Grows – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: As your company expands, it's crucial to make quality improvements in areas like team naming, documentation, monitoring, standardization of tools, and measuring performance through metrics. These changes help streamline operations and communication, preventing issues that arise from increased complexity in larger organizations.

recent_posts.title: Testathon – Think Like a Tester
recent_posts.summary: Testathon is an event designed to encourage exploratory testing among team members, including software testers, engineers, managers, and product owners. Participants test various products in teams over two days and log bugs, which are then reproduced and evaluated by judges. The event fosters collaboration, highlights the importance of detailed bug reports, and results in valuable bug discoveries, including critical security and usability issues. The initiative has received positive feedback and emphasizes the significance of exploratory testing in improving product quality.
